title: How to hear this sermon
english: This is a listening version of John Wesley's sermon, Upon Our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse Four. It is the sermon as printed in John Wesley's 1771 Works. Rendered in modern English.

title: The salt of the earth
english: You are the salt of the earth (Matthew 5:13). But if the salt has lost its savor, with what shall it be salted? It is from then on good for nothing, but to be cast out and trodden under foot by people. Matthew 5:13.

title: The light of the world
english: You are the light of the world. A city that is set on a hill cannot be hidden (Matthew 5:14). Matthew 5:14.

title: The candle
english: Nor do people light a candle and put it under a bushel (Matthew 5:15), but on a candlestick, and it gives light to all who are in the house. Matthew 5:15.

title: Let your light shine
english: Let your light so shine before people, that they may see your good works (Matthew 5:16), and glorify your Father who is in heaven. Matthew 5:16.

title: The beauty of holiness
english: The beauty of holiness, of that inward person of the heart, who is renewed after the image of God, cannot but strike every eye which God has opened, every enlightened understanding. The ornament of a meek, humble, loving spirit will at least win the approval of all who are able, in any degree, to tell spiritual good from evil. From the hour people begin to come out of the darkness which covers the giddy, unthinking world, they cannot but see how desirable a thing it is to be thus transformed into the likeness of him who created us. This inward religion bears the shape of God so visibly stamped upon it that a soul must be wholly sunk in flesh and blood when he can doubt its divine origin. We may say of this, in a secondary sense, even as of the Son of God himself, that it is the brightness of his glory, the exact image of his person (Hebrews 1:3), the beaming forth of his eternal glory, and yet so tempered and softened that even the children of men may here see God and live. It is the character, the stamp, the living impression of his person, who is the fountain of beauty and love, the original source of all excellence and perfection.

title: Why load it with doing
english: If religion, then, were carried no further than this, they could have no doubt about it. They would have no objection to pursuing it with the whole ardor of their souls. But why, they say, is it clogged with other things? What need is there of loading it with doing and suffering? These are what damp the vigor of the soul and sink it down to earth again. Is it not enough to follow after love? To soar on the wings of love? Will it not be enough to worship God, who is a Spirit, with the spirit of our minds, without burdening ourselves with outward things, or even thinking of them at all? Is it not better that the whole reach of our thoughts should be taken up with high and heavenly contemplation, and that, instead of busying ourselves at all about outward things, we should only commune with God in our hearts?

title: Cease from outward actions
english: Many eminent men have spoken this way. They have advised us to cease from all outward actions, wholly to withdraw from the world, to leave the body behind us, to abstract ourselves from all sensible things, to have no concern at all about outward religion, but to work all virtues in the will, as the far more excellent way, more perfecting of the soul, as well as more acceptable to God.

title: The wisdom from beneath
english: It was not needed that anyone should tell our Lord of this masterpiece of the wisdom from beneath (James 3:15), this fairest of all the devices with which Satan has ever perverted the right ways of the Lord. And oh, what instruments he has found, from time to time, to employ in this service of his, to wield this grand engine of hell against some of the most important truths of God. Men who would deceive, if it were possible, the very elect (Matthew 24:24), the men of faith and love. Yes, who have for a season deceived and led away no small number of them, who have fallen in every age into the gilded snare, and hardly escaped with the skin of their teeth (Job 19:20).

title: His answer
english: But has our Lord been wanting on his part? Has he not guarded us enough against this pleasing delusion? Has he not armed us here with armor of proof against Satan transformed into an angel of light (2 Corinthians 11:14)? Yes, truly. He here defends, in the clearest and strongest manner, the active, patient religion he had just described. What can be fuller and plainer than the words he immediately adds to what he had said of doing and suffering? You are the salt of the earth (Matthew 5:13). But if the salt has lost its savor, with what shall it be salted? It is from then on good for nothing, but to be cast out and trodden under foot by people. Matthew 5:13. You are the light of the world. A city that is set on a hill cannot be hidden (Matthew 5:14). Matthew 5:14. Nor do people light a candle and put it under a bushel (Matthew 5:15), but on a candlestick, and it gives light to all who are in the house. Matthew 5:15. Let your light so shine before people, that they may see your good works (Matthew 5:16) and glorify your Father who is in heaven. Matthew 5:16.

title: What this sermon will show
english: In order fully to explain and press these important words, I shall try to show, first, that Christianity is essentially a social religion, and that to turn it into a solitary one is to destroy it. Second, that to conceal this religion is impossible, as well as utterly contrary to the design of its Author. I shall, third, answer some objections, and conclude the whole with a practical application.

title: A social religion
english: First, I shall try to show that Christianity is essentially a social religion, and that to turn it into a solitary religion is indeed to destroy it.

title: What Christianity means
english: By Christianity I mean that way of worshipping God which is here revealed to man by Jesus Christ. When I say this is essentially a social religion, I mean not only that it cannot exist so well, but that it cannot exist at all without society, without living and talking with other people. And in showing this, I shall confine myself to those considerations which will arise from the very discourse before us. But if this is shown, then without doubt to turn this religion into a solitary one is to destroy it.

title: Solitude and society
english: Not that we can in any way condemn the mixing of solitude or retirement with society. This is not only allowable but useful. Indeed, it is necessary, as daily experience shows, for everyone who either already is, or desires to be, a real Christian. It can hardly be that we should spend one entire day in a continued intercourse with people without suffering loss in our soul, and in some measure grieving the Holy Spirit of God. We need daily to retire from the world, at least morning and evening, to talk with God, to commune more freely with our Father who is in secret (Matthew 6:6). Nor indeed can a person of experience condemn even longer seasons of religious retirement, so long as they do not imply any neglect of the worldly work in which the providence of God has placed us.

title: Retirement must not swallow our time
english: Yet such retirement must not swallow up all our time. This would be to destroy, not advance, true religion. For that the religion described by our Lord in the foregoing words cannot exist without society, without our living and talking with other people, is plain from this, that several of its most essential branches can have no place if we have no intercourse with the world.

title: Meekness
english: There is no disposition, for instance, which is more essential to Christianity than meekness. Now although this, as it implies resignation to God, or patience in pain and sickness, may exist in a desert, in a hermit's cell, in total solitude, yet as it implies, which it no less necessarily does, mildness, gentleness, and long-suffering, it cannot possibly have a being. It has no place under heaven without an intercourse with other people. So that to attempt turning this into a solitary virtue is to destroy it from the face of the earth.

title: Peacemaking
english: Another necessary branch of true Christianity is peacemaking, or doing good. That this is equally essential with any of the other parts of the religion of Jesus Christ, there can be no stronger argument to prove, and therefore it would be absurd to bring any other, than that it is here inserted in the original plan he has laid down of the fundamentals of his religion. Therefore to set this aside is the same daring insult to the authority of our great Master as to set aside mercy, purity of heart, or any other branch of his institution. But this is plainly set aside by all who call us to the wilderness, who recommend entire solitude either to the babes, or the young men, or the fathers in Christ. For will anyone affirm that a solitary Christian, so called, though it is little less than a contradiction in terms, can be a merciful person, that is, one who takes every opportunity of doing all good to all people? What can be plainer than that this fundamental branch of the religion of Jesus Christ cannot possibly exist without society, without our living and talking with other people?

title: Company with good people only
english: But is it not useful, however, one might naturally ask, to talk only with good people, only with those whom we know to be meek and merciful, holy of heart and holy of life? Is it not useful to refrain from any conversation or intercourse with people of the opposite character, people who do not obey, perhaps do not believe, the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ? The advice of Saint Paul to the Christians at Corinth may seem to favor this. I wrote to you in a letter not to company with fornicators (1 Corinthians 5:9). And it is certainly not advisable so to company with them, or with any of the workers of iniquity, as to have any particular familiarity, or any closeness of friendship with them. To contract or continue an intimacy with any such is in no way useful for a Christian. It must necessarily expose him to a great many dangers and snares, out of which he can have no reasonable hope of deliverance.

title: Not to go out of the world
english: But the apostle does not forbid us to have any intercourse at all, even with the people who do not know God. For then, he says, you would have to go out of the world (1 Corinthians 5:10), which he could never advise them to do. But he adds, If any man who is called a brother, who professes himself a Christian, is a fornicator, or covetous, or an idolater, or a railer, or a drunkard, or an extortioner (1 Corinthians 5:11), now I have written to you not to keep company with him, with such a one, no, not to eat. This must necessarily imply that we break off all familiarity, all intimacy of acquaintance with them. Yet do not count him as an enemy, but admonish him as a brother (2 Thessalonians 3:15). The apostle plainly shows that even in such a case as this we are not to renounce all fellowship with him. So that here is no advice to separate wholly, even from wicked people. Yes, these very words teach us quite the contrary.

title: Commerce with the world
english: Much more the words of our Lord, who is so far from directing us to break off all commerce with the world that, without it, according to his account of Christianity, we cannot be Christians at all. It would be easy to show that some intercourse even with ungodly and unholy people is absolutely necessary for the full exercise of every temper which he has described as the way to the kingdom. It is indispensably necessary for the complete exercise of poverty of spirit, of mourning, and of every other disposition which has a place here in the genuine religion of Jesus Christ. Yes, it is necessary to the very being of several of them. Of that meekness, for example, which, instead of demanding an eye for an eye, or a tooth for a tooth (Matthew 5:38), does not resist evil, but causes us rather, when struck on the right cheek, to turn the other also (Matthew 5:39). Of that mercy by which we love our enemies, bless those who curse us, do good to those who hate us (Matthew 5:44), and pray for those who spitefully use us and persecute us. And of that mingling of love and all holy tempers which is exercised in suffering for righteousness' sake. Now all these, it is clear, could have no being if we were to have no commerce with any but real Christians.

title: Season what is around you
english: Indeed, if we were wholly to separate ourselves from sinners, how could we possibly answer that character which our Lord gives us in these very words? You Christians, you who are lowly, serious, and meek, you who hunger after righteousness, who love God and man, who do good to all and therefore suffer evil, you are the salt of the earth. It is your very nature to season whatever is around you. It is the nature of the divine savor which is in you to spread to whatever you touch, to diffuse itself on every side to all those among whom you are. This is the great reason why the providence of God has so mingled you together with other people, that whatever grace you have received of God may through you be passed on to others, that every holy temper and word and work of yours may have an influence on them also. By this means a check will, in some measure, be given to the corruption which is in the world, and a small part at least saved from the general infection, and made holy and pure before God.

title: If the salt has lost its savor
english: That we may the more diligently labor to season all we can with every holy and heavenly temper, our Lord goes on to show the desperate state of those who do not pass on the religion they have received, which indeed they cannot possibly fail to do so long as it remains in their own hearts. If the salt has lost its savor, with what shall it be salted? It is from then on good for nothing but to be cast out and trodden under foot by people. If you who were holy and heavenly-minded, and therefore zealous of good works, have no longer that savor in yourselves, and therefore no longer season others, if you have grown flat, insipid, dead, both careless of your own soul and useless to the souls of other people, with what shall you be salted? How shall you be recovered? What help? What hope? Can tasteless salt be restored to its savor? No. It is from then on good for nothing but to be cast out, even as the mire in the streets, and to be trodden under foot by people, to be overwhelmed with everlasting contempt. If you had never known the Lord, there might have been hope, if you had never been found in him. But what can you now say to that solemn declaration of his, just parallel to what he has spoken here? Every branch in me that does not bear fruit (John 15:2), he, the Father, takes away. He who abides in me, and I in him, bears much fruit (John 15:5). If a man does not abide in me, or does not bear fruit, he is cast out as a branch and withered (John 15:6), and people gather them, not to plant them again, but to cast them into the fire.

title: Those who turn back
english: Toward those who have never tasted the good word, God is indeed pitiful and of tender mercy. But justice takes place with regard to those who have tasted that the Lord is gracious (1 Peter 2:3), and have afterward turned back from the holy commandment (2 Peter 2:21) then delivered to them. For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened (Hebrews 6:4), in whose hearts God had once shone, to enlighten them with the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ (2 Corinthians 4:6), who have tasted the heavenly gift, of redemption in his blood, the forgiveness of sins (Ephesians 1:7), and were made partakers of the Holy Spirit, of lowliness, of meekness, and of the love of God and of man shed abroad in their hearts by the Holy Spirit who was given to them, and have fallen away, here is not a supposition but a flat declaration of fact, to renew them again to repentance, seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh and put him to an open shame (Hebrews 6:6).

title: Who these words concern
english: But so that none may misunderstand these awful words, it should be carefully observed, first, who they are that are spoken of here, namely they, and they only, who were once thus enlightened. They only who did taste that heavenly gift and were thus made partakers of the Holy Spirit. So that all who have not experienced these things are wholly unconcerned in this scripture. Second, what that falling away is which is spoken of here. It is an absolute, total apostasy. A believer may fall, and not fall away. He may fall and rise again. And if he should fall, even into sin, yet this case, dreadful as it is, is not desperate. For we have an Advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous (1 John 2:1), and he is the propitiation for our sins (1 John 2:2). But let him above all things beware, lest his heart be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin (Hebrews 3:13), lest he should sink lower and lower until he wholly falls away, until he becomes as salt that has lost its savor. For if we thus sin willfully, after we have received the experimental knowledge of the truth, there remains no more sacrifice for sins (Hebrews 10:26), but a certain fearful looking for of fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries (Hebrews 10:27).

title: May it be done in secret
english: But although we may not wholly separate ourselves from mankind, although it is granted we ought to season them with the religion which God has worked in our hearts, yet may this not be done without being noticed? May we not pass this on to others in a secret and almost imperceptible manner, so that scarcely anyone shall be able to observe how or when it is done? Even as salt passes its own savor into that which is seasoned by it, without any noise, and without being open to any outward observation. And if so, although we do not go out of the world (1 Corinthians 5:10), yet we may lie hidden in it. We may thus far keep our religion to ourselves, and not offend those whom we cannot help.

title: Flesh and blood
english: Our Lord was well aware also of this plausible reasoning of flesh and blood. And he has given a full answer to it in those words which come now to be considered. In explaining them I shall try to show, as I proposed to do in the second place, that so long as true religion abides in our hearts, it is impossible to conceal it, as well as absolutely contrary to the design of its great Author.

title: A city on a hill
english: And first, it is impossible for any who have it to conceal the religion of Jesus Christ. Our Lord makes this plain beyond all contradiction by a twofold comparison. You are the light of the world. A city set upon a hill cannot be hidden.

title: Love cannot be hidden
english: You Christians are the light of the world, with regard both to your tempers and your actions. Your holiness makes you as conspicuous as the sun in the midst of heaven. As you cannot go out of the world (1 Corinthians 5:10), so neither can you stay in it without appearing to all mankind. You may not flee from people, and while you are among them it is impossible to hide your lowliness and meekness, and those other dispositions by which you aspire to be perfect, as your Father who is in heaven is perfect (Matthew 5:48). Love cannot be hidden any more than light, and least of all when it shines out in action, when you exercise yourselves in the labor of love, in kindness of every kind. People might as well think to hide a city as to hide a Christian. Yes, they might as well conceal a city set upon a hill (Matthew 5:14) as a holy, zealous, active lover of God and man.

title: They will call the light darkness
english: It is true, people who love darkness rather than light, because their deeds are evil (John 3:19), will take all possible pains to prove that the light which is in you is darkness (Matthew 6:23). They will say evil, every kind of evil, falsely, of the good which is in you. They will lay to your charge that which is farthest from your thoughts, which is the very reverse of all you are and all you do. And your patient continuance in well-doing (Romans 2:7), your meek suffering of all things for the Lord's sake, your calm, humble joy in the midst of persecution, your unwearied labor to overcome evil with good (Romans 12:21), will make you still more visible and conspicuous than you were before.

title: A secret religion is not Christianity
english: So impossible it is to keep our religion from being seen, unless we cast it away. So vain is the thought of hiding the light, unless by putting it out. It is sure that a secret, unobserved religion cannot be the religion of Jesus Christ. Whatever religion can be concealed is not Christianity. If a Christian could be hidden, he could not be compared to a city set upon a hill (Matthew 5:14), to the light of the world, the sun shining from heaven and seen by all the world below. Never, therefore, let it enter into the heart of him whom God has renewed in the spirit of his mind (Ephesians 4:23) to hide that light, to keep his religion to himself, especially considering it is not only impossible to conceal true Christianity, but likewise absolutely contrary to the design of the great Author of it.

title: Not under a bushel
english: This plainly appears from the following words. Nor do people light a candle to put it under a bushel (Matthew 5:15). As if he had said, as people do not light a candle only to cover and conceal it, so neither does God enlighten any soul with his glorious knowledge and love, to have it covered or concealed, either by prudence falsely so called, or shame, or voluntary humility, to have it hidden either in a desert or in the world, either by avoiding people or in talking with them. But they put it on a candlestick, and it gives light to all who are in the house. In the same way, it is the design of God that every Christian should be in an open point of view, that he may give light to all around, that he may visibly express the religion of Jesus Christ.

title: Lights in a dark place
english: Thus God has in every age spoken to the world, not only by precept but by example also. He has not left himself without witness (Acts 14:17) in any nation where the sound of the gospel has gone forth, without a few who testified to his truth by their lives as well as their words. These have been as lights shining in a dark place (2 Peter 1:19). And from time to time they have been the means of enlightening some, of preserving a remnant, a little seed, which was counted to the Lord for a generation (Psalm 22:30). They have led a few poor sheep out of the darkness of the world and guided their feet into the way of peace (Luke 1:79).

title: The depths of Satan
english: One might imagine that where both scripture and the reason of things speak so clearly and expressly, there could not be much advanced on the other side, at least not with any appearance of truth. But those who imagine this know little of the depths of Satan (Revelation 2:24). After all that scripture and reason have said, so exceedingly plausible are the pretenses for solitary religion, for a Christian's going out of the world, or at least hiding himself in it, that we need all the wisdom of God to see through the snare, and all the power of God to escape it. So many and strong are the objections which have been brought against being social, open, active Christians.

title: Religion is in the heart
english: To answer these was the third thing which I proposed. And first, it has often been objected that religion does not lie in outward things, but in the heart, the inmost soul, that it is the union of the soul with God, the life of God in the soul of man, that outside religion is nothing worth, seeing God does not delight in burnt offerings (Psalm 51:16), in outward services, but a pure and holy heart is the sacrifice he will not despise (Psalm 51:17).

title: The root puts forth branches
english: I answer, it is most true that the root of religion lies in the heart, in the inmost soul, that this is the union of the soul with God, the life of God in the soul of man. But if this root is really in the heart, it cannot but put forth branches. And these are the several instances of outward obedience, which partake of the same nature with the root, and consequently are not only marks or signs, but substantial parts of religion.

title: Outside religion
english: It is also true that bare outside religion, which has no root in the heart, is nothing worth, that God does not delight in such outward services, no more than in Jewish burnt offerings, and that a pure and holy heart is a sacrifice with which he is always well pleased. But he is also well pleased with all that outward service which arises from the heart, with the sacrifice of our prayers, whether public or private, of our praises and thanksgivings, with the sacrifice of our goods, humbly devoted to him and employed wholly to his glory, and with that of our bodies, which he particularly claims, which the apostle begs us, by the mercies of God, to present to him, a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God (Romans 12:1).

title: Love is all in all
english: A second objection, closely related to this, is that love is all in all, that it is the fulfilling of the law (Romans 13:10), the end of the commandment (1 Timothy 1:5), of every commandment of God, that all we do and all we suffer, if we do not have love, profits us nothing, and that therefore the apostle directs us to follow after love, and calls this the more excellent way.

title: Love constrains us to obey
english: I answer, it is granted that the love of God and of man, arising from sincere faith, is all in all, the fulfilling of the law (Romans 13:10), the end of every commandment of God (1 Timothy 1:5). It is true that without this, whatever we do, whatever we suffer, profits us nothing. But it does not follow that love is all in such a sense as to set aside either faith or good works. It is the fulfilling of the law (Romans 13:10), not by releasing us from it, but by constraining us to obey it. It is the end of the commandment (1 Timothy 1:5), as every commandment leads to and centers in it. It is allowed that whatever we do or suffer without love profits us nothing. But at the same time, whatever we do or suffer in love, though it were only the suffering of reproach for Christ, or the giving of a cup of cold water in his name (Matthew 10:42), it shall in no way lose its reward.

title: Follow after love
english: But does not the apostle direct us to follow after love? And does he not call it a more excellent way? He does direct us to follow after love, but not after that alone. His words are, Follow after love, and desire spiritual gifts (1 Corinthians 14:1). Yes, follow after love, and desire to spend and to be spent (2 Corinthians 12:15) for your brothers and sisters. Follow after love, and as you have opportunity, do good to all people (Galatians 6:10).

title: A more excellent way
english: In the same verse also, in which he calls this, the way of love, a more excellent way, he directs the Corinthians to desire other gifts besides it, yes, to desire them earnestly. Earnestly desire, he says, the best gifts, and yet I show you a more excellent way (1 Corinthians 12:31). More excellent than what? Than the gifts of healing, of speaking with tongues (1 Corinthians 12:28), and of interpreting, mentioned in the preceding verse. But not more excellent than the way of obedience. Of this the apostle is not speaking. Neither is he speaking of outward religion at all. So that this text is quite wide of the present question.

title: God has joined them
english: But suppose the apostle had been speaking of outward as well as inward religion, and comparing them together. Suppose in the comparison he had given the preference ever so much to the latter. Suppose he had preferred, as he justly might, a loving heart before all outward works whatever. Yet it would not follow that we were to reject either one or the other. No. God has joined them together (Matthew 19:6) from the beginning of the world. And let not man put them asunder (Matthew 19:6).

title: God is a Spirit
english: But God is a Spirit, and those who worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth (John 4:24). And is not this enough? Indeed, ought we not to employ the whole strength of our mind in this? Does not attending to outward things clog the soul, so that it cannot soar aloft in holy contemplation? Does it not damp the vigor of our thought? Has it not a natural tendency to burden and distract the mind? Whereas Saint Paul would have us be without anxiety, and wait upon the Lord without distraction.

title: Worship in spirit and in truth
english: I answer, God is a Spirit, and those who worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth (John 4:24). Yes, and this is enough. We ought to employ the whole strength of our mind in this. But then I would ask, What is it to worship God, a Spirit, in spirit and in truth? Why, it is to worship him with our spirit, to worship him in that manner which none but spirits are capable of. It is to believe in him as a wise, just, holy being, of purer eyes than to behold iniquity (Habakkuk 1:13), and yet merciful, gracious, and long-suffering, forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin (Exodus 34:7), casting all our sins behind his back (Isaiah 38:17), and accepting us in the Beloved (Ephesians 1:6). It is to love him, to delight in him, to desire him, with all our heart and mind and soul and strength (Mark 12:30), to imitate him we love by purifying ourselves even as he is pure (1 John 3:3), and to obey him whom we love and in whom we believe, both in thought and word and work. Consequently, one branch of worshipping God in spirit and in truth is the keeping of his outward commandments. To glorify him, therefore, with our bodies as well as with our spirits (1 Corinthians 6:20), to go through outward work with hearts lifted up to him, to make our daily employment a sacrifice to God, to buy and sell, to eat and drink to his glory (1 Corinthians 10:31), this is worshipping God in spirit and in truth, as much as praying to him in a wilderness.

title: Contemplation is one way
english: But if so, then contemplation is only one way of worshipping God in spirit and in truth. Therefore to give ourselves up entirely to this would be to destroy many branches of spiritual worship, all equally acceptable to God and equally profitable, not hurtful, to the soul. For it is a great mistake to suppose that an attention to those outward things to which the providence of God has called us is any clog to a Christian, or any hindrance at all to his always seeing him who is invisible (Hebrews 11:27). It does not at all damp the ardor of his thought. It does not burden or distract his mind. It gives him no uneasy or hurtful care, who does it all as to the Lord, who has learned, whatever he does in word or deed, to do all in the name of the Lord Jesus (Colossians 3:17), having only one eye of the soul, which moves around on outward things, and one immovably fixed on God. Learn what this means (Matthew 9:13), you poor recluses, so that you may clearly see your own littleness of faith. Yes, so that you may no longer judge others by yourselves, go and learn what this means (Matthew 9:13).

title: The hymn
english: You, O Lord, in tender love, bear all my burdens. Lift my heart to things above, and fix it ever there. Calm on the wheel of tumult I sit, among busy multitudes alone, sweetly waiting at your feet, till all your will is done.

title: We appeal to experience
english: But the grand objection is still behind. We appeal, they say, to experience. Our light did shine. We used outward things for many years, and yet they profited nothing. We attended all the ordinances, but we were no better for it, nor indeed anyone else. No, we were the worse. For we fancied ourselves Christians for doing so, when we did not know what Christianity meant.

title: The abuse and the use
english: I allow the fact. I allow that you, and ten thousand more, have thus abused the ordinances of God, mistaking the means for the end, supposing that the doing of these, or some other outward works, either was the religion of Jesus Christ, or would be accepted in the place of it. But let the abuse be taken away, and the use remain. Now use all outward things, but use them with a constant eye to the renewal of your soul in righteousness and true holiness.

title: Lost labor
english: But this is not all. They affirm, Experience likewise shows that the trying to do good is but lost labor. What does it avail to feed or clothe people's bodies if they are just dropping into everlasting fire? And what good can anyone do to their souls? If these are changed, God does it himself. Besides, all people are either good, at least desirous to be so, or obstinately evil. Now the former have no need of us. Let them ask help of God, and it shall be given them. And the latter will receive no help from us. No, and our Lord forbids us to cast our pearls before swine (Matthew 7:6).

title: Feed the hungry
english: I answer, first, whether they will finally be lost or saved, you are expressly commanded to feed the hungry and clothe the naked (Matthew 25:35). If you can, and do not, whatever becomes of them, you shall go away into everlasting fire (Matthew 25:41). Second, though it is God only who changes hearts, yet he generally does it by man. It is our part to do all that lies in us, as diligently as if we could change them ourselves, and then to leave the event to him. Third, God, in answer to their prayers, builds up his children by each other in every good gift, nourishing and strengthening the whole body by that which every joint supplies. So that the eye cannot say to the hand, I have no need of you (1 Corinthians 12:21), no, nor even the head to the feet, I have no need of you. Lastly, how are you sure that the persons before you are dogs or swine? Do not judge them until you have tried. How do you know, man, but you may gain your brother? But you may, under God, save his soul from death (James 5:20)? When he spurns your love and blasphemes the good word, then it is time to give him up to God.

title: We have tried
english: We have tried. We have labored to reform sinners. And what did it avail? On many we could make no impression at all. And if some were changed for a while, yet their goodness was but as the morning dew (Hosea 6:4), and they were soon as bad, no, worse than ever. So that we only hurt them, and ourselves too, for our minds were hurried and unsettled, perhaps filled with anger instead of love. Therefore we had better have kept our religion to ourselves.

title: Sow your seed
english: It is very possible this fact also may be true, that you have tried to do good and have not succeeded, yes, that those who seemed reformed relapsed into sin, and their last state was worse than the first (Matthew 12:45). And what wonder? Is the servant above his Master (John 13:16)? But how often did he strive to save sinners, and they would not hear, or when they had followed him a while, they turned back as a dog to his vomit (2 Peter 2:22). But he did not therefore stop striving to do good. No more should you, whatever your success is. It is your part to do as you are commanded. The event is in the hand of God. You are not accountable for this. Leave it to him who orders all things well. In the morning sow your seed, and in the evening do not withhold your hand, for you do not know which shall prosper. Ecclesiastes 11:6.

title: Seventy times seven
english: But the trial hurries and frets your own soul. Perhaps it did so for this very reason, because you thought you were accountable for the event, which no one is, nor indeed can be. Or perhaps because you were off your guard. You were not watchful over your own spirit. But this is no reason for disobeying God. Try again, but try more carefully than before. Do good, as you forgive, not seven times only, but until seventy times seven (Matthew 18:22). Only be wiser by experience. Attempt it every time more cautiously than before. Be more humbled before God, more deeply convinced that of yourself you can do nothing. Be more jealous over your own spirit, more gentle, and watchful in prayer. Thus cast your bread upon the waters (Ecclesiastes 11:1), and you shall find it again after many days.

title: Let your light so shine before people
english: Notwithstanding all these plausible pretenses for hiding it, let your light so shine before people, that they may see your good works (Matthew 5:16) and glorify your Father who is in heaven. This is the practical application which our Lord himself makes of the foregoing considerations.

title: Do not conceal it
english: Let your light so shine. Your lowliness of heart, your gentleness and meekness of wisdom, your serious, weighty concern for the things of eternity, and sorrow for the sins and miseries of people, your earnest desire of universal holiness and full happiness in God, your tender good will to all mankind, and fervent love to your supreme benefactor. Try not to conceal this light with which God has enlightened your soul, but let it shine before people, before all with whom you are, in the whole course of your conversation. Let it shine still more eminently in your actions, in your doing all possible good to all people, and in your suffering for righteousness' sake, while you rejoice and are very glad, knowing that great is your reward in heaven (Matthew 5:12).

title: Not your own praise
english: Let your light so shine before people, that they may see your good works (Matthew 5:16). So far let a Christian be from ever designing or desiring to conceal his religion. On the contrary, let it be your desire not to conceal it, not to put the light under a bushel (Matthew 5:15). Let it be your care to place it on a candlestick, that it may give light to all who are in the house. Only take heed not to seek your own praise in this, not to desire any honor to yourselves. But let it be your sole aim that all who see your good works may glorify your Father who is in heaven.

title: Without dissimulation
english: Let this be your one final end in all things. With this view, be plain, open, undisguised. Let your love be without dissimulation (Romans 12:9). Why should you hide fair, disinterested love? Let no deceit be found in your mouth (1 Peter 2:22). Let your words be the genuine picture of your heart. Let there be no darkness or reserve in your conversation, no disguise in your behavior. Leave this to those who have other designs in view, designs which will not bear the light. Be artless and simple to all mankind, that all may see the grace of God which is in you. And although some will harden their hearts, yet others will take knowledge that you have been with Jesus (Acts 4:13), and, by returning themselves to the great Bishop of their souls (1 Peter 2:25), glorify your Father who is in heaven.

title: Stand alone
english: With this one design, that people may glorify God in you, go on in his name and in the power of his might (Ephesians 6:10). Do not be ashamed even to stand alone, so long as it is in the ways of God. Let the light which is in your heart shine in all good works, both works of piety and works of mercy. And in order to enlarge your ability of doing good, renounce all superfluities. Cut off all unnecessary expense in food, in furniture, in clothing. Be a good steward of every gift of God, even of these his lowest gifts. Cut off all unnecessary expense of time, all needless or useless employments. And whatever your hand finds to do, do it with your might (Ecclesiastes 9:10). In a word, be full of faith and love. Do good. Suffer evil. And in this be steadfast, immovable, yes, always abounding in the work of the Lord, since you know that your labor is not in vain in the Lord (1 Corinthians 15:58).
